data.narrative:
Last Energy, a Series C nuclear energy company founded by Bret Kugelmass, has raised $140M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader nuclear energy comp universe of 11 peers (3 public, 8 private), including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, though direct same-stage comparables remain limited.

A stage-progression method was the primary applicable approach, applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement to the $140M total raised proxy, yielding $238M. The peer-median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient narrow-set peers meeting same-stage or adjacent-stage criteria; six nuclear energy peers exist in the broader universe, but fewer than three align closely enough on stage and tier to support robust median triangulation without introducing significant bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $202M to $274M, with a median point of $238M. Key uncertainties center on the thinness of direct-stage comparables in the nuclear subsector, which limits peer-based cross-validation. The range reflects plausible variance around stage-typical progression mechanics rather than consensus pricing signals from a mature peer set. Additional valuation confidence would require either emergence of closer same-stage nuclear comps or successful deployment milestones that anchor fundamental value.
